053/**
054 * A class encapsulating <a
055 * href="https://jakarta.ee/specifications/cdi/4.0/jakarta-cdi-spec-4.0#performing_typesafe_resolution">CDI-compatible
056 * type matching rules</a>.
057 *
058 * @author <a href="https://about.me/lairdnelson/" target="_top">Laird Nelson</a>
059 *
060 * @see #matches(TypeMirror, TypeMirror)
061 */
062public class TypeMatcher implements Constable {
063
064
065  /*
066   * Instance fields.
067   */
068
069
070  private final TypeAndElementSource tes;
071
072
073  /*
074   * Constructors.
075   */
076
077
078  /**
079   * Creates a new {@link TypeMatcher}.
080   *
081   * @param tes a {@link TypeAndElementSource}; must not be {@code null}
082   *
083   * @exception NullPointerException if {@code tes} is {@code null}
084   *
085   * @see TypeAndElementSource
086   */
087  public TypeMatcher(final TypeAndElementSource tes) {
088    super();
089    this.tes = Objects.requireNonNull(tes, "tes");
090  }
091
092
093  /*
094   * Instance methods.
095   */
096
097
098  /*
099   * Public methods.
100   */
101
102  /**
103   * Returns an {@link Optional} housing a {@link ConstantDesc} that represents this {@link TypeMatcher}.
104   *
105   * <p>This method never returns {@code null}. Overrides must not return {@code null}.</p>
106   *
107   * <p>Subclasses of {@link TypeMatcher} that add internal state will almost certainly have to override this
108   * method.</p>
109   *
110   * <p>The default implementation of this method relies on the presence of a {@code public} constructor that accepts a
111   * single {@link TypeAndElementSource}-typed argument.</p>
112   *
113   * <p>The {@link Optional} returned by an invocation of this method may be, and often will be, {@linkplain
114   * Optional#isEmpty() empty}.</p>
115   *
116   * @return an {@link Optional} housing a {@link ConstantDesc} that represents this {@link TypeMatcher}; never {@code
117   * null}
118   *
119   * @see Constable#describeConstable()
120   */
121  @Override // Constable
122  public Optional<? extends ConstantDesc> describeConstable() {
123    return (this.tes instanceof Constable c ? c.describeConstable() : Optional.<ConstantDesc>empty())
124      .map(tesDesc -> DynamicConstantDesc.of(BSM_INVOKE,
125                                             MethodHandleDesc.ofConstructor(ClassDesc.of(this.getClass().getName()),
126                                                                            CD_TypeAndElementSource),
127                                             tesDesc));
128  }
129
130  /**
131   * Returns {@code true} if and only if the supplied {@code payload} argument <a
132   * href="https://jakarta.ee/specifications/cdi/4.0/jakarta-cdi-spec-4.0#performing_typesafe_resolution"><em>matches</em></a>
133   * the supplied {@code receiver} argument, according to the rules defined by <a
134   * href="https://jakarta.ee/specifications/cdi/4.0/jakarta-cdi-spec-4.0#performing_typesafe_resolution">section
135   * 2.4.2.1 of the CDI specification</a>.
136   *
137   * @param receiver the left hand side of a type assignment; must not be {@code null}
138   *
139   * @param payload the right hand side of a type assignment; must not be {@code null}
140   *
141   * @return {@code true} if and only if the supplied {@code payload} argument <a
142   * href="https://jakarta.ee/specifications/cdi/4.0/jakarta-cdi-spec-4.0#performing_typesafe_resolution">matches</a>
143   * the supplied {@code receiver} argument, according to the rules defined by <a
144   * href="https://jakarta.ee/specifications/cdi/4.0/jakarta-cdi-spec-4.0#performing_typesafe_resolution">section
145   * 2.4.2.1 of the CDI specification</a>; {@code false} otherwise
146   *
147   * @exception NullPointerException if either argument is {@code null}
148   */
149  // Is the payload assignable to the receiver? That is, does the payload "match the receiver", in CDI parlance?
150  public boolean matches(final TypeMirror receiver, final TypeMirror payload) {
151    // "A bean is assignable to a given injection point if:
152    //
153    // "The bean has a bean type [payload] that matches the required type [receiver]. For this purpose..."
154    return receiver == Objects.requireNonNull(payload, "payload") || switch (receiver.getKind()) {
155      // "...primitive types are considered to match their corresponding wrapper types in java.lang..."
156      case BOOLEAN  -> payload.getKind() == TypeKind.BOOLEAN || declaredTypeNamed(payload, "java.lang.Boolean");
157      case BYTE     -> payload.getKind() == TypeKind.BYTE    || declaredTypeNamed(payload, "java.lang.Byte");
158      case CHAR     -> payload.getKind() == TypeKind.CHAR    || declaredTypeNamed(payload, "java.lang.Character");
159      case DOUBLE   -> payload.getKind() == TypeKind.DOUBLE  || declaredTypeNamed(payload, "java.lang.Double");
160      case FLOAT    -> payload.getKind() == TypeKind.FLOAT   || declaredTypeNamed(payload, "java.lang.Float");
161      case INT      -> payload.getKind() == TypeKind.INT     || declaredTypeNamed(payload, "java.lang.Integer");
162      case LONG     -> payload.getKind() == TypeKind.LONG    || declaredTypeNamed(payload, "java.lang.Long");
163      case SHORT    -> payload.getKind() == TypeKind.SHORT   || declaredTypeNamed(payload, "java.lang.Short");
164      // "...and array types are considered to match only if their element types [note: not component types] are
165      // identical ['identical' is actually undefined in the specification]..."
166      case ARRAY    -> payload.getKind() == TypeKind.ARRAY   && this.identical(elementType(receiver), elementType(payload));
167      case DECLARED -> switch (payload.getKind()) {
168        // "...primitive types are considered to match ['match' is not strictly defined in the specification; it is just
169        // assumed the reader knows what is meant] their corresponding wrapper types in java.lang..."
170        case BOOLEAN  -> named((DeclaredType)receiver, "java.lang.Boolean");
171        case BYTE     -> named((DeclaredType)receiver, "java.lang.Byte");
172        case CHAR     -> named((DeclaredType)receiver, "java.lang.Character");
173        case DOUBLE   -> named((DeclaredType)receiver, "java.lang.Double");
174        case FLOAT    -> named((DeclaredType)receiver, "java.lang.Float");
175        case INT      -> named((DeclaredType)receiver, "java.lang.Integer");
176        case LONG     -> named((DeclaredType)receiver, "java.lang.Long");
177        case SHORT    -> named((DeclaredType)receiver, "java.lang.Short");
178        // "Parameterized and raw types [and non-generic classes, and non-array types]..."
179        case DECLARED ->
180          // "...are considered to match if they are identical [undefined]..."
181          this.identical(receiver, payload) ||
182          // "...or if the bean type [payload] is assignable to [see #assignable(TypeMirror, TypeMirror)] the required type
183          // [receiver]...."
184          this.assignable((DeclaredType)receiver, (DeclaredType)payload);
185        default       -> throw new IllegalArgumentException("Illegal payload kind: " + payload.getKind() + "; payload: " + payload);
186      };
187      default       -> throw new IllegalArgumentException("Illegal receiver kind: " + receiver.getKind() + "; receiver: " + receiver);
188    };
189  }
190
191  /**
192   * Returns the {@link TypeAndElementSource} used by this {@link TypeMatcher}.
193   *
194   * @return the {@link TypeAndElementSource} used by this {@link TypeMatcher}; never {@code null}
195   *
196   * @see #TypeMatcher(TypeAndElementSource)
197   *
198   * @see TypeAndElementSource
199   */
200  public final TypeAndElementSource typeAndElementSource() {
201    return this.tes;
202  }
203
204  /*
205   * Private methods.
206   */
207
208  private final boolean assignable(final DeclaredType receiver, final DeclaredType payload) {
209    assert receiver.getKind() == TypeKind.DECLARED;
210    assert payload.getKind() == TypeKind.DECLARED;
211    return switch (payload) {
212      // "A parameterized bean type [payload] is considered assignable..."
213      case DeclaredType parameterizedPayload when parameterized(payload) -> switch (receiver) {
214        // "...to a [non-generic class or] raw required type [receiver]..."
215        case TypeMirror rawReceiver when !generic(receiver) || raw(receiver) -> {
216          // "...if the [non-generic class or] raw types are identical [undefined] and all type parameters [type
217          // arguments] of the bean type [payload] are either unbounded type variables [undefined] or java.lang.Object."
218          yield
219            this.identical(this.nonGenericClassOrRawType(rawReceiver), this.nonGenericClassOrRawType(parameterizedPayload)) &&
220            allTypeArgumentsAre(parameterizedPayload.getTypeArguments(),
221                                ((Predicate<TypeMirror>)this::unboundedTypeVariable).or(TypeMatcher::isJavaLangObject));
222        }
223        // "...to a parameterized required type [receiver]..."
224        case DeclaredType parameterizedReceiver when parameterized(receiver) -> {
225          // "...if they have identical raw type [really if their declarations/elements are 'identical']..."
226          if (this.identical(this.rawType(parameterizedReceiver), this.rawType(parameterizedPayload))) {
227            // "...and for each parameter [type argument pair]..."
228            final List<? extends TypeMirror> rtas = parameterizedReceiver.getTypeArguments();
229            final List<? extends TypeMirror> ptas = parameterizedPayload.getTypeArguments();
230            assert rtas.size() == ptas.size();
231            for (int i = 0; i < rtas.size(); i++) {
232              final TypeMirror rta = rtas.get(i);
233              final TypeMirror pta = ptas.get(i);
234              // "...the required [receiver] type parameter [type argument] and the bean [payload] type parameter [type
235              // argument] are actual types [non-type variable, non-wildcard reference types]..."
236              if (actual(rta)) {
237                if (actual(pta)) {
238                  // "...with identical [non-generic classes or] raw type[s]..."
239                  if (this.identical(this.nonGenericClassOrRawType(rta), this.nonGenericClassOrRawType(pta))) {
240                    // "...and, if the type [?] is parameterized [?]..."
241                    //
242                    // Let rta and pta be array types with parameterized element types, such as List<Number>[] and
243                    // List<String>[]. Then their raw types are List[] and List[]. Their parameterized element types are
244                    // List<Number> and List<String>. According to the JLS, neither List<Number>[] nor List<String>[] is
245                    // parameterized.
246                    //
247                    // In this example, if we get here, we have only proven that List[] is "identical" to List[].
248                    //
249                    // The "if the type is parameterized" clause is tough. Which type is under discussion? "the type"
250                    // seems to refer to the "identical raw type". But a raw type by definition is not parameterized, so
251                    // this clause would seem to be superfluous and thus never apply, and so List<Number>[] :=
252                    // List<String>[] is OK. Oops. So not that interpretation.
253                    //
254                    // What if instead the "if the type is parameterized" clause means the receiver type itself and
255                    // somehow loosely the payload type as well? Well, clearly it cannot correctly do this, since an
256                    // array type is never a parameterized type. Same bad result. Oops. So not that interpretation.
257                    //
258                    // Or what if "identical raw type" really means "identical raw type (or identical component type if
259                    // they are array types)"? That would be most efficient, since it would rule out List<Number>[] :=
260                    // List<String>[] right off the bat: we wouldn't even get here. But that really doesn't seem to be
261                    // what is meant. So probably not that interpretation.
262                    //
263                    // What if the "if the type is parameterized" clause really means "if the element type declaration
264                    // used by both the receiver and payload types is generic"? That would work. That's also
265                    // semantically equivalent to something like: "...if at least one of the two arguments is a
266                    // parameterized type [e.g. List<Number>, not List<Number>[], not String, not List], or at least one
267                    // of the two types is an array type with a parameterized element type [e.g. List<Number>[], not
268                    // List[], not String[]]..."
269                    //
270                    // That is the interpretation we apply here. So:
271                    //
272                    //   "...and, if the type [?] is parameterized [?]..."
273                    //
274                    // becomes:
275                    //
276                    //   "...and, if at least one of the two type arguments is a parameterized type, or if at least one
277                    //   of the two types is an array type with a parameterized element type..."
278                    //
279                    // That, in turn, designates any type capable of properly yielding a raw type, while ruling out
280                    // those that can't! That means it is exactly equal to our yieldsRawType(TypeMirror) method, and so
281                    // that's what cdiParameterized(TypeMirror) returns (go see for yourself).
282                    if (cdiParameterized(rta)) { // really just yieldsRawType(rta)
283                      assert cdiParameterized(pta); // ...because otherwise their raw types would not have been "identical"
284                      // "...the bean type parameter [type argument] is assignable to the required type parameter [type
285                      // argument] according to [all of] these rules [including 'matching']..."
286                      if (matches(rta, pta)) {
287                        continue;
288                      }
289                      yield false;
290                    } else {
291                      assert !cdiParameterized(pta);
292                      continue; // yes, trust me; vetted
293                    }
294                  }
295                  yield false;
296                } else if (pta.getKind() == TypeKind.TYPEVAR) {
297                  // "...the required [receiver] type parameter [type argument] is an actual type [a non-type variable,
298                  // non-wildcard reference type], the bean [payload] type parameter [type argument] is a type variable and
299                  // the actual type [non-type variable, non-wildcard reference type] [required type argument, receiver] is
300                  // assignable to the upper bound, if any, of the type variable [bean type argument, payload] [type
301                  // variables have multiple bounds]..."
302                  if (assignableToCondensedTypeVariableBounds((TypeVariable)pta, (ReferenceType)rta)) {
303                    continue;
304                  }
305                  yield false;
306                }
307                throw new AssertionError("Unexpected payload type argument kind: " + pta.getKind());
308              } else if (rta.getKind() == TypeKind.WILDCARD) {
309                // "...the required type parameter [type argument] is a wildcard, the bean type parameter [type
310                // argument] is an actual type [a non-type variable, non-wildcard reference type]..."
311                if (actual(pta)) {
312                  // "...and the actual type [non-type variable, non-wildcard reference type] is assignable to the upper
313                  // bound, if any, of the wildcard and assignable from the lower bound, if any of the wildcard"
314                  if (assignableToCondensedExtendsBound((WildcardType)rta, (ReferenceType)pta) &&
315                      assignableFromCondensedSuperBound((ReferenceType)pta, (WildcardType)rta)) {
316                    continue;
317                  }
318                  yield false;
319                } else if (pta.getKind() == TypeKind.TYPEVAR) {
320                  // "...the required [receiver] type parameter [type argument] is a wildcard, the bean [payload] type
321                  // parameter [type argument] is a type variable and the upper bound of the type variable [a type
322                  // variable has many bounds?] is assignable to or assignable from the upper bound, if any, of the
323                  // wildcard and assignable from the lower bound, if any, of the wildcard"
324                  if ((condensedTypeVariableBoundsAssignableToCondensedExtendsBound((WildcardType)rta, (TypeVariable)pta) ||
325                       condensedTypeVariableBoundsAssignableFromCondensedExtendsBound((TypeVariable)pta, (WildcardType)rta)) &&
326                      condensedTypeVariableBoundsAssignableFromCondensedSuperBound((TypeVariable)pta, (WildcardType)rta)) {
327                    continue;
328                  }
329                  yield false;
330                }
331                throw new AssertionError("Unexpected payload type argument kind: " + pta.getKind());
332              } else if (rta.getKind() == TypeKind.TYPEVAR) {
333                if (pta.getKind() == TypeKind.TYPEVAR) {
334                  // "...the required [receiver] type parameter [type argument] and the bean [payload] type parameter
335                  // [type argument] are both type variables and the upper bound of the required [receiver] type
336                  // parameter [type argument] [a type variable has many bounds?] is assignable to the upper bound [a
337                  // type variable has many bounds?], if any, of the bean [payload] type parameter [type argument]"
338                  if (condensedTypeVariableBoundsAssignableToCondensedTypeVariableBounds((TypeVariable)pta, (TypeVariable)rta)) {
339                    continue;
340                  }
341                  yield false;
342                }
343                throw new AssertionError("Unexpected payload type argument kind: " + pta.getKind());
344              }
345              throw new AssertionError("Unexpected receiver type argument kind: " + rta.getKind());
346            }
347            yield true; // we passed all the type argument assignability tests
348          }
349          yield false; // the type arguments' non-generic classes or raw types were not identical
350        }
351        default -> throw new AssertionError("Unexpected receiver kind: " + receiver.getKind());
352      };
353      // "A [non-generic or] raw bean type [payload] is considered assignable..."
354      case TypeMirror nonGenericOrRawPayload -> switch (receiver) {
355        // "...to a parameterized required type [receiver]..."
356        case DeclaredType parameterizedReceiver when parameterized(receiver) -> {
357          // "...if the[ir] [non-generic classes or] raw types are identical and all type parameters [type arguments] of
358          // the required type [receiver] are either unbounded type variables or java.lang.Object."
359          yield
360            this.identical(this.nonGenericClassOrRawType(parameterizedReceiver), nonGenericOrRawPayload) &&
361            allTypeArgumentsAre(parameterizedReceiver.getTypeArguments(),
362                                ((Predicate<TypeMirror>)this::unboundedTypeVariable).or(TypeMatcher::isJavaLangObject));
363        }
364        // [Otherwise the payload is not assignable to the receiver; identity checking should have already happened in
365        // matches(), not here.]
366        case DeclaredType nonGenericOrRawReceiver when receiver.getKind() == TypeKind.DECLARED -> {
367          yield false; // or yield this.identical(nonGenericOrRawReceiver, nonGenericOrRawPayload);
368        }
369        default -> throw new AssertionError("Unexpected payload kind: " + payload.getKind() + "; receiver: " + receiver + "; payload: " + payload);
370      };
371    };
372  }
373
374  // Is payload "identical to" receiver, following the intent of CDI? The relation "identical to" is not defined in the
375  // specification. Does it mean ==? Does it mean equals()? Does it mean
376  // javax.lang.model.util.Types#isSameType(TypeMirror, TypeMirror)? Something else?
377  //
378  // This implementation chooses TypeAndElementSource#sameType(TypeMirror, TypeMirror), but with one
379  // change. TypeAndElementSource#sameType(TypeMirror, TypeMirror) is usually backed by the
380  // javax.lang.model.util.Types#isSameType(TypeMirror, TypeMirror) method. That method will return false if either
381  // argument is a wildcard type. This method first checks to see if the arguments are identical (==), regardless of
382  // type.
383  private final boolean identical(final TypeMirror receiver, final TypeMirror payload) {
384    // CDI has an undefined notion of "identical to". This method attempts to divine and implement the intent. Recall
385    // that javax.lang.model.* compares types with "sameType" semantics.
386    return receiver == payload || this.tes.sameType(receiver, payload);
387  }
388
389  // Is the "actual" type argument represented by payload assignable to all of the receiver's condensed bounds?
390  //
391  // Pay close attention to how this is called, i.e. what is payload and what is receiver is often "backwards". For
392  // example:
393  //
394  //   @Inject Foo<String> foo; <-- Bean<T extends CharSequence> // is the String "actual type" (payload) assignable to T's (receiver's) CharSequence bound?
395  //   //          ^ payload!            ^ receiver!
396  //
397  // Recall that after condensing "T extends CharSequence" you get CharSequence.
398  //
399  // Recall that if, instead, you had T extends S and S extends CharSequence, condensing T still yields CharSequence.
400  private final boolean assignableToCondensedTypeVariableBounds(final TypeVariable receiver, final ReferenceType payload) {
401    assert receiver.getKind() == TypeKind.TYPEVAR;
402    assert actual(payload); // We can assert this only because of where the method is called.
403    return covariantlyAssignable(List.of(receiver), List.of(payload)); // deliberately List.of(payload) and not condense(payload)
404  }
405
406  // Is candidate covariantly assignable to w's condensed extends (upper) bound?
407  private final boolean assignableToCondensedExtendsBound(final WildcardType w, final ReferenceType candidate) {
408    assert w.getKind() == TypeKind.WILDCARD;
409    assert actual(candidate); // We can assert this only because of where this method is called from.
410    final ReferenceType extendsBound = (ReferenceType)w.getExtendsBound();
411    return extendsBound == null || switch (extendsBound.getKind()) {
412    case ARRAY, DECLARED -> covariantlyAssignable(extendsBound, candidate);
413    case TYPEVAR -> covariantlyAssignable((ReferenceType)this.condense(extendsBound), List.of(candidate));
414    default -> throw new AssertionError();
415    };
416  }
417
418  // It's not immediately clear what CDI means by a type variable's upper bound. In javax.lang.model.type parlance, the
419  // upper bound of a TypeVariable could be an IntersectionType, which java.lang.reflect.TypeVariable represents as a
420  // collection of bounds. CDI blundered into this earlier: https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CDI-440 and
421  // https://github.com/jakartaee/cdi/issues/682
422  //
423  // "the upper bound of the required type parameter [receiver type argument] is assignable to the upper bound, if any,
424  // of the bean type parameter [payload type argument]" (when both arguments are type variables) should *actually*
425  // read:
426  //
427  // "for each bound, PTA, of the bean type parameter [payload type argument], there is at least one bound, RTA, of the
428  // required type parameter [receiver type argument], which is assignable to PTA."
429  //
430  // The TCK enforces this, even though it's not in the specification (!).
431  //
432  // Weld's implementation confuses type parameters with arguments, just like the specification. They have a series of
433  // methods implemented as part of PR 614 (https://github.com/weld/core/pull/614) named "parametersMatch" [arguments
434  // match].
435  //
436  // Weld also has methods named things like "getUppermostTypeVariableBounds" and "getUppermostBounds". These appear to
437  // "condense" useless type variable extensions to "get to" the "real" types involved. So T extends S extends String
438  // becomes String.
439  //
440  // Digging deeper, you (I) might think getUppermostTypeVariableBounds(tv) is just erase(tv) applied recursively. But I
441  // think you would be wrong.
442  //
443  // Start with:
444  // https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/181845ae46157a9bb3bf8e2a328fa59eddc0273a/src/jdk.compiler/share/classes/com/sun/tools/javac/code/Types.java#L2450
445  //
446  // Compare vs.:
447  // https://github.com/weld/core/blob/e894d1699ff1c91332605f5ecae5f53410effb81/impl/src/main/java/org/jboss/weld/resolution/AbstractAssignabilityRules.java#L57-L62
448  //
449  // To illustrate the difference between the two operations, recursive erasure (according to the Java Language
450  // Specification) of the pseudo-declaration T extends S extends List<String> & Serializable would yield, simply, List
451  // (T would erease to "the erasure of its leftmost bound", which would be the erasure of S, which would be "the
452  // erasure of its leftmost bound", which would be the erasure of List<String>, which would be List. Serializable just
453  // gets dropped.)
454  //
455  // By contrast, Weld's getUppermostTypeVariableBounds(T) operation would yield [List<String>, Serializable] (have not
456  // tested this with code, just reading).
457  //
458  // I think this is what the javac compiler calls, somewhat confusingly, "classBound":
459  // https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/jdk-24%2B7/src/jdk.compiler/share/classes/com/sun/tools/javac/code/Types.java#L2760-L2796
460  //
461  // So then:
462  //
463  // For every bound in (condensed) receiverBounds, is there a bound in (condensed) payloadBounds that is covariantly
464  // assignable to it?
465  //
466  // (Is there one bound in (condensed) payloadBounds that matches all bounds in (condensed) receiver bounds?)
467  //
468  // Throws ClassCastException if, after condensing, any encountered bound is not either an ArrayType or a DeclaredType.
469  private final boolean covariantlyAssignable(final List<? extends TypeMirror> receiverBounds, List<? extends TypeMirror> payloadBounds) {
470    payloadBounds = this.condense(payloadBounds);
471    for (final TypeMirror condensedReceiverBound : this.condense(receiverBounds)) {
472      if (!covariantlyAssignable((ReferenceType)condensedReceiverBound, payloadBounds)) {
473        return false;
474      }
475    }
476    return true;
477  }
478
479  // Is there a DeclaredType-or-ArrayType bound in condensedPayloadBounds that is assignable to classOrArrayTypeReceiver
480  // using Java, not CDI, assignability semantics?
481  //
482  // It is assumed condensedPayloadBounds is the result of a condense() call.
483  //
484  // Throws ClassCastException or IllegalArgumentException if any encountered type is neither an ArrayType nor a
485  // DeclaredType.
486  private final boolean covariantlyAssignable(final ReferenceType classOrArrayTypeReceiver, final List<? extends TypeMirror> condensedPayloadBounds) {
487    assert actual(classOrArrayTypeReceiver); // We can assert this only because of where this method is called.
488    return switch (classOrArrayTypeReceiver.getKind()) {
489    case ARRAY, DECLARED -> {
490      for (final TypeMirror condensedPayloadBound : condensedPayloadBounds) {
491        assert actual(condensedPayloadBound);
492        if (covariantlyAssignable(classOrArrayTypeReceiver, (ReferenceType)condensedPayloadBound)) {
493          yield true;
494        }
495      }
496      yield false;
497    }
498    default -> throw new IllegalArgumentException("classOrArrayTypeReceiver: " + classOrArrayTypeReceiver + "; kind: " + classOrArrayTypeReceiver.getKind());
499    };
500  }
501
502  // Is classOrArrayTypePayload assignable to classOrArrayTypeReceiver following the rules of Java assignability
503  // (i.e. covariance)?
504  //
505  // The types are ReferenceTypes because this is only ever invoked in the context of type arguments.
506  private final boolean covariantlyAssignable(final ReferenceType classOrArrayTypeReceiver, final ReferenceType classOrArrayTypePayload) {
507    assert actual(classOrArrayTypeReceiver); // Based on where and how this method is called.
508    assert actual(classOrArrayTypePayload); // Based on where and how this method is called.
509    return
510      classOrArrayTypeReceiver == classOrArrayTypePayload || // Optimization
511      // Note that TypeAndElementSource#assignable(TypeMirror, TypeMirror) follows the lead of
512      // javax.lang.model.util.Types#isAssignable(TypeMirror, TypeMirror) where the "payload" is the *first* parameter
513      // and the "receiver" is the *second* argument.
514      this.tes.assignable(classOrArrayTypePayload, classOrArrayTypeReceiver); // yes, "backwards"
515  }
516
517  // Are payload's condensed bounds assignable to receiver's condensed extends bound (upper bound)?
518  private final boolean condensedTypeVariableBoundsAssignableToCondensedExtendsBound(final WildcardType receiver, final TypeVariable payload) {
519    assert receiver.getKind() == TypeKind.WILDCARD;
520    assert payload.getKind() == TypeKind.TYPEVAR;
521    // "...the upper bound of the type variable [a type variable has many bounds?] is assignable TO [...] the upper
522    // bound, if any, of the wildcard..."
523    final TypeMirror extendsBound = receiver.getExtendsBound();
524    // No need to condense arguments to eliminate useless type variables and intersection types so that Java covariant
525    // semantics will work properly in this case; #covariantlyAssignable(List, List) does this already.
526    return extendsBound == null || covariantlyAssignable(List.of((ReferenceType)extendsBound), List.of(payload));
527  }
528
529  // Is payload's condensed extends bound (upper bound) covariantly assignable to receiver's condensed bounds?
530  private final boolean condensedTypeVariableBoundsAssignableFromCondensedExtendsBound(final TypeVariable receiver, final WildcardType payload) {
531    assert receiver.getKind() == TypeKind.TYPEVAR;
532    assert payload.getKind() == TypeKind.WILDCARD;
533    // "...the upper bound of the type variable [a type variable has many bounds?] is assignable [...] FROM the upper
534    // bound, if any, of the wildcard..."
535    final TypeMirror extendsBound = payload.getExtendsBound();
536    // No need to condense arguments to eliminate useless type variables and intersection types so that Java covariant
537    // semantics will work properly in this case; #covariantlyAssignable(List, List) does this already.
538    return extendsBound == null || covariantlyAssignable(List.of(receiver), List.of((ReferenceType)extendsBound));
539  }
540
541  // Is payload's super bound (lower bound) covariantly assignable to receiver's condensed bounds?
542  private final boolean condensedTypeVariableBoundsAssignableFromCondensedSuperBound(final TypeVariable receiver, final WildcardType payload) {
543    assert receiver.getKind() == TypeKind.TYPEVAR;
544    assert payload.getKind() == TypeKind.WILDCARD;
545    final TypeMirror superBound = payload.getSuperBound();
546    // No need to condense arguments to eliminate useless type variables and intersection types so that Java covariant
547    // semantics will work properly in this case; #covariantlyAssignable(List, List) does this already.
548    return superBound == null || covariantlyAssignable(List.of(receiver), List.of(superBound));
549  }
550
551  // Are payload's condensed bounds covariantly assignable to receiver's condensed bounds?
552  private final boolean condensedTypeVariableBoundsAssignableToCondensedTypeVariableBounds(final TypeVariable receiver, final TypeVariable payload) {
553    assert receiver.getKind() == TypeKind.TYPEVAR;
554    assert payload.getKind() == TypeKind.TYPEVAR;
555    // No need to condense arguments to eliminate useless type variables and intersection types so that Java covariant
556    // semantics will work properly in this case; #covariantlyAssignable(List, List) does this already.
557    return covariantlyAssignable(List.of(receiver), List.of(payload));
558  }
559
560  // Is payload's condensed super bound (lower bound) covariantly assignable to receiver?
561  //
562  // Since either of a wildcard type's bounds may be a type variable, and since a type variable's bound may be an
563  // intersection type, it follows that after condensation either of a wildcard type's bounds may be a list of actual
564  // types.
565  //
566  // Therefore this is really: Is there one bound among payload's actual super bounds that is assignable to receiver?
567  private final boolean assignableFromCondensedSuperBound(final ReferenceType receiver, final WildcardType payload) {
568    assert payload.getKind() == TypeKind.WILDCARD;
569    assert actual(receiver); // We can assert this only because of where this method is called from.
570    final ReferenceType superBound = (ReferenceType)payload.getSuperBound();
571    return superBound == null || switch (superBound.getKind()) {
572    case ARRAY, DECLARED -> covariantlyAssignable(receiver, superBound);
573    case TYPEVAR -> covariantlyAssignable(receiver, (ReferenceType)this.condense(superBound));
574    default -> throw new AssertionError();
575    };
576  }
577
578  // Get the raw type yielded by t, assuming t is the sort of type that can yield a raw type.
579  //
580  // An array type with a parameterized element type can yield a raw type.
581  //
582  // A declared type that is parameterized can yield a raw type.
583  //
584  // No other type yields a raw type.
585  //
586  // t cannot be null.
587  private final TypeMirror rawType(final TypeMirror t) {
588    return switch (t.getKind()) {
589    case ARRAY -> {
590      final TypeMirror et = elementType(t);
591      if (!parameterized(et)) {
592        throw new IllegalArgumentException("t is an array type whose element type is not parameterized so cannot yield a raw type");
593      }
594      yield this.arrayTypeOf(this.erasure(et));
595    }
596    case DECLARED -> {
597      if (!parameterized(t)) {
598        throw new IllegalArgumentException("t is a declared type that is not parameterized so cannot yield a raw type");
599      }
600      yield this.erasure(t);
601    }
602    default -> throw new IllegalArgumentException("t is a " + t.getKind() + " type and so cannot yield a raw type");
603    };
604  }
605
606  // Return t if its element declares a non-generic class, or if it is the raw type usage of a generic class.
607  private final TypeMirror nonGenericClassOrRawType(final TypeMirror t) {
608    return yieldsRawType(t) ? this.rawType(t) : t;
609  }
610
611  // Erase t and return its erasure. Erasing is a complex business that can involve the creation of new types.
612  private final TypeMirror erasure(final TypeMirror t) {
613    return this.tes.erasure(t);
614  }
615
616  // Return a possibly new ArrayType whose component type is the supplied componentType.
617  private final ArrayType arrayTypeOf(final TypeMirror componentType) {
618    return this.tes.arrayTypeOf(componentType);
619  }
620
621  // "Condenses" t, according to the following rules.
622  //
623  // If t is null, returns List.of().
624  //
625  // If t is a type variable, returns the result of condensing its upper bound (thus eliminating the type variable).
626  //
627  // If t is an intersection type, returns the result of condensing its bounds (thus eliminating the intersection type).
628  //
629  // If t is a wildcard type, returns the result of condensing either its super or extends bound (thus eliminating the
630  // wildcard type). The result of condensing a wildcard type that declares neither bound (?) is the result of
631  // condensing the type declared by java.lang.Object.
632  //
633  // In all other cases returns List.of(t).
634  //
635  // Note especially this is not type erasure, though it has some similarities.
636  //
637  // See #condense(List) below.
638  private final List<? extends TypeMirror> condense(final TypeMirror t) {
639    return t == null ? List.of() : switch (t.getKind()) {
640    case INTERSECTION -> this.condense(((IntersectionType)t).getBounds());
641    case TYPEVAR      -> this.condense(((TypeVariable)t).getUpperBound());
642    case WILDCARD     -> {
643      final WildcardType w = (WildcardType)t;
644      final TypeMirror s = w.getSuperBound();
645      final TypeMirror e = w.getExtendsBound();
646      if (s == null) {
647        yield e == null ? List.of(this.tes.declaredType("java.lang.Object")) : this.condense(e);
648      } else if (e == null) {
649        yield this.condense(s);
650      } else {
651        throw new AssertionError();
652      }
653    }
654    default           -> List.of(t); // t's bounds are defined solely by itself, or it's a wildcard and we didn't say which bounds
655    };
656  }
657
658  // If ts is empty, returns an empty unmodifiable List.
659  //
660  // If ts consists of a single element, returns the result of condensing t (see #condense(TypeMirror) above).
661  //
662  // Otherwise creates a new list, condenses each element of ts, and adds each element of the condensation to the new
663  // list, and returns an unmodifiable view of the new list.
664  //
665  // Note that deliberately duplicates are not eliminated from the new list.
666  private final List<? extends TypeMirror> condense(final List<? extends TypeMirror> ts) {
667    final int size = ts.isEmpty() ? 0 : ts.size();
668    if (size == 0) {
669      return List.of();
670    }
671    // We take care not to allocate/copy new lists needlessly.
672    ArrayList<TypeMirror> newBounds = null;
673    for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
674      final TypeMirror t = ts.get(i);
675      switch (t.getKind()) {
676      case INTERSECTION:
677      case TYPEVAR:
678      case WILDCARD:
679        // These are the only types where condensing does anything. In these cases alone we need to make a new list.
680        if (newBounds == null) {
681          newBounds = new ArrayList<>(size * 2);
682          if (i > 0) {
683            // All ts up to this point have been non-condensable types, so catch up and add them as-is.
684            newBounds.addAll(ts.subList(0, i));
685          }
686        }
687        newBounds.addAll(condense(t));
688        break;
689      default:
690        if (newBounds != null) {
691          newBounds.add(t);
692        }
693        break;
694      }
695    }
696    if (newBounds == null) {
697      return ts;
698    }
699    newBounds.trimToSize();
700    return Collections.unmodifiableList(newBounds);
701  }
702
703  // Is t an unbounded type variable?
704  //
705  // CDI does not define what an "unbounded type variable" is. This method attempts to divine and implement the intent.
706  //
707  // Since according to the Java Language Specification, all type variables have an upper bound, which in the
708  // pathological case is java.lang.Object, it would seem that "unbounded" means "has java.lang.Object as its upper
709  // bound".
710  //
711  // It is not clear in the case of T extends S whether T is an unbounded TypeVariable or not. This interpretation
712  // behaves as if it is.
713  //
714  // Weld seems to take the position that an unbounded type variable is one that has java.lang.Object as its sole upper
715  // bound; see
716  // https://github.com/weld/core/blob/5.1.2.Final/impl/src/main/java/org/jboss/weld/util/Types.java#L258. Under this
717  // interpretation T extends S would not be considered an unbounded type variable. Type variable bounds are erased in
718  // every other situation in CDI.
719  private final boolean unboundedTypeVariable(final TypeMirror t) {
720    return switch (t.getKind()) {
721    case TYPEVAR -> {
722      final List<? extends TypeMirror> condensedBounds = this.condense(((TypeVariable)t).getUpperBound());
723      yield condensedBounds.size() == 1 && isJavaLangObject(condensedBounds.get(0));
724    }
725    default -> false;
726    };
727  }
728
729
730  /*
731   * Static methods.
732   */
733
734
735  // Does e represent a generic declaration?
736  //
737  // A declaration is generic if it declares one or more type parameters.
738  //
739  // Since an annotation interface cannot declare type parameters, it follows that TypeElements representing annotation
740  // instances are never generic.
741  private static final boolean generic(final Element e) {
742    return switch (e.getKind()) {
743    case CLASS, CONSTRUCTOR, ENUM, INTERFACE, METHOD, RECORD -> !((Parameterizable)e).getTypeParameters().isEmpty();
744    default -> false;
745    };
746  }
747
748  // Is t the usage of a generic class, i.e. a usage (whether raw or parameterized) of a generic class declaration?
749  //
750  // t is deemed to be generic if it is a declared type whose defining element (its type declaration) is generic.
751  //
752  // Array types are never generic.
753  private static final boolean generic(final TypeMirror t) {
754    return
755      t.getKind() == TypeKind.DECLARED &&
756      generic(((DeclaredType)t).asElement());
757  }
758
759  // Is t a parameterized type (and not a raw type) strictly according to the rules of the Java Language Specification?
760  //
761  // A type is parameterized if it is a declared type with a non-empty list of type arguments. No other type is
762  // parameterized.
763  private static final boolean parameterized(final TypeMirror t) {
764    return
765      t.getKind() == TypeKind.DECLARED &&
766      !((DeclaredType)t).getTypeArguments().isEmpty();
767  }
768
769  // Is t a type that CDI considers to be "parameterized"?
770  //
771  // There are some cases, but not all, where CDI (incorrectly) considers an array type to be something that can be
772  // parameterized, or else "bean type parameter" resolution would never work. See
773  // https://stackoverflow.com/questions/76493672/when-cdi-speaks-of-a-parameterized-type-does-it-also-incorrectly-mean-array-typ.
774  //
775  // The semantics CDI wants to express are really: can t yield a raw type? See #yieldsRawType(TypeMirror) below.
776  private static final boolean cdiParameterized(final TypeMirror t) {
777    return yieldsRawType(t);
778  }
779
780  // Can t yield a raw type?
781  //
782  // To yield a raw type, t must be either:
783  //
784  // * an array type with a parameterized element type
785  // * a declared type with at least one type argument
786  private static final boolean yieldsRawType(final TypeMirror t) {
787    return parameterized(t) || t.getKind() == TypeKind.ARRAY && parameterized(elementType(t));
788  }
789
790  // Is t a raw type, following the rules of the Java Language Specification, not CDI?
791  //
792  // A raw type is either "the erasure of a parameterized type" (so List<String>'s raw type is List, clearly not
793  // List<?>, and not List<E>) or "an array type whose element type is a raw type" (so List<String>[]'s raw type is
794  // List[]). (String is not a raw type; its element defines no type parameters.)
795  //
796  // No other type is a raw type.
797  //
798  // CDI gets confused and uses "raw" in different senses. The sense used here is that of the Java Language
799  // Specification.
800  private static final boolean raw(final TypeMirror t) {
801    return switch (t.getKind()) {
802    case ARRAY -> raw(elementType((ArrayType)t));
803    case DECLARED -> generic(t) && ((DeclaredType)t).getTypeArguments().isEmpty();
804    case TYPEVAR -> false; // called out explicitly just so you realize it
805    default -> false;
806    };
807  }
808
809  // Is t a declared type that bears the supplied fully qualified name?
810  private static final boolean declaredTypeNamed(final TypeMirror t, final CharSequence n) {
811    return
812      t.getKind() == TypeKind.DECLARED &&
813      named(((DeclaredType)t), n);
814  }
815
816  // Regardless of its reported TypeKind, does t's declaring TypeElement bear the supplied fully qualified name?
817  //
818  // Throws ClassCastException if the return value of t.asElement() is not a TypeElement.
819  private static final boolean named(final DeclaredType t, final CharSequence n) {
820    // (No getKind() check on purpose.)
821    return ((QualifiedNameable)t.asElement()).getQualifiedName().contentEquals(n);
822  }
823
824  // Do all supplied TypeMirrors, when used as type arguments, pass the test represented by the supplied Predicate?
825  private static final boolean allTypeArgumentsAre(final Iterable<? extends TypeMirror> typeArguments, final Predicate<? super TypeMirror> p) {
826    for (final TypeMirror t : typeArguments) {
827      if (!p.test(t)) {
828        return false;
829      }
830    }
831    return true;
832  }
833
834  // Is e a TypeElement representing java.lang.Object?
835  private static final boolean isJavaLangObject(final Element e) {
836    return
837      e.getKind() == ElementKind.CLASS &&
838      ((QualifiedNameable)e).getQualifiedName().contentEquals("java.lang.Object");
839  }
840
841  // Is t a DeclaredType whose asElement() method returns an Element representing java.lang.Object?
842  private static final boolean isJavaLangObject(final TypeMirror t) {
843    return
844      t.getKind() == TypeKind.DECLARED &&
845      isJavaLangObject(((DeclaredType)t).asElement());
846  }
847
848  // Is t an "actual type"?
849  //
850  // CDI mentions actual types but does not define what they are. This method attempts to divine and implement the
851  // intent.
852  //
853  // A comment in a closed bug report (CDI-502)
854  // (https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CDI-502?focusedId=13036118&page=com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.issuetabpanels%3Acomment-tabpanel#comment-13036118)
855  // by one of the reference implementation's authors (Jozef Hartinger) provides the only definition:
856  //
857  // "An actual type is a type that is not a wildcard nor [sic] an unresolved [sic] type variable."
858  //
859  // The Java Language Specification does not mention anything about "actual types" or type variable "resolution". CDI
860  // does not mention anything about type variable "resolution".
861  //
862  // (Clearly type variable "resolution" must simply be the process of supplying a type argument for a type parameter.)
863  //
864  // Presumably the null type is not intended to be an actual type either.
865  //
866  // More strictly, therefore, the intent seems to be that an actual type is an array, declared or primitive type, and
867  // none other.
868  //
869  // See also: https://github.com/weld/core/blob/5.1.2.Final/impl/src/main/java/org/jboss/weld/util/Types.java#L213
870  private static final boolean actual(final TypeMirror t) {
871    return switch (t.getKind()) {
872    case ARRAY, BOOLEAN, BYTE, CHAR, DECLARED, DOUBLE, FLOAT, INT, LONG, SHORT -> true;
873    default -> false;
874    };
875  }
876
877  // Returns the element type of t.
878  //
879  // The element type of an array type is the element type of its component type.
880  //
881  // The element type of every other kind of type is the type itself.
882  private static final TypeMirror elementType(final TypeMirror t) {
883    return t.getKind() == TypeKind.ARRAY ? elementType(((ArrayType)t).getComponentType()) : t;
884  }
885
886}
